title: Henselianity of valuation coarsenings
statement: Let $K$ be a field and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Suppose that $V$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. If $U\subseteq K$ is another valuation ring with $V\subseteq U$, then $U$ is henselian. The inclusion $V\subseteq U$ is called a coarsening of valuations; $U=K$ is allowed. No rank, discreteness, completeness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: valued-field background for the reference to Bourbaki, A.C., VI, §8. Coarsening input for comparing topologically equivalent base valuations; Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra VI §8, henselian valuations and compositions, WANTED. ILO supplies the motivating valued-field comparison, not a proof of this permanence theorem.

proof.text: For either valuation subring $A=V,U$, the nonunits form its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Indeed, for nonzero nonunits $x,y$, the valuation condition gives $x/y\in A$ or $y/x\in A$, so $x+y=y(1+x/y)$ or $x(1+y/x)$ is a nonunit. Zero and additive inverses cause no problem, and a multiple of a nonunit is a nonunit. Thus the nonunits form a proper ideal, while every proper ideal contains only nonunits. This proves locality directly from [def-trf-valuation-ring].

proof.text: We have $\mathfrak m_U\subseteq\mathfrak m_V$ as subsets of $K$: if $0\ne x\in\mathfrak m_U$ were outside $V$, then $x^{-1}\in V\subseteq U$, a contradiction; and a unit of $V$ is a unit of $U$. For any $c\in U$, choose $s_c=1$ if $c\in V$ and $s_c=c^{-1}$ otherwise. In the second case $c^{-1}\in V$ and both $c,c^{-1}$ lie in $U$. Hence in both cases $s_c\in V\cap U^\times$ and $s_cc\in V$. For finitely many $c_i\in U$, their product $s=\prod_i s_{c_i}$ lies in $V\cap U^\times$ and satisfies $sc_i\in V$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tags 00IB (lemma-valuation-ring-x-or-x-inverse), 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian); direct agent coefficient-rescaling argument, not a proof attributed to ILO.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], it suffices to lift every simple residue root of every monic $F\in U[T]$. Let $\alpha\in U/\mathfrak m_U$ be such a root and choose a representative $a\in U$. Then $F(a)\in\mathfrak m_U$ and $d=F'(a)\in U^\times$. If $F(a)=0$, the required lift is $a$. Otherwise set $n=\deg F\geq1$ and expand
$$h(X)=d^{-1}F(a+X)=c_0+X+\sum_{i=2}^n c_iX^i.$$
All $c_i$ lie in $U$ and $0\ne c_0=d^{-1}F(a)\in\mathfrak m_U$.

source.place: Tags 00IB (lemma-valuation-ring-x-or-x-inverse), 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian); direct agent coefficient-rescaling argument, not a proof attributed to ILO.

proof.text:
Choose $s\in V\cap U^\times$ as in Step 2 for the finite list $c_2,\ldots,c_n$ (take $s=1$ for an empty list). Put $b_0=c_0/s$ and $b_i=c_i s^{i-1}$ for $i\geq2$. Then $0\ne b_0\in\mathfrak m_U\subseteq\mathfrak m_V$, and $b_i=(sc_i)s^{i-2}\in V$. Thus
$$g(X)=s^{-1}h(sX)=b_0+X+\sum_{i=2}^n b_iX^i\in V[X].$$
Although $g$ need not be monic, the explicit polynomial
$$Q(Y)=Y^n+Y^{n-1}+\sum_{i=2}^n b_i b_0^{i-1}Y^{n-i}\in V[Y]$$
is monic. Its reduction is $Y^{n-1}(Y+1)$, whose root $-1$ has derivative $(-1)^{n-1}\ne0$ in every residue characteristic, also for $n=1$.

source.place: Tags 00IB (lemma-valuation-ring-x-or-x-inverse), 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian); direct agent coefficient-rescaling argument, not a proof attributed to ILO.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] to the henselian local ring $V$, the monic polynomial $Q$, and the simple residue root $-1$. Obtain $y\in V$ with $Q(y)=0$ and $y\equiv-1\pmod{\mathfrak m_V}$. In particular $y\in V^\times\subseteq U^\times$. Set $z=b_0/y\in\mathfrak m_U$. The explicit formula of Step 4 gives, inside $K$,
$$Q(y)=\frac{y^n}{b_0}\,g\!\left(\frac{b_0}{y}\right).$$
Since $b_0\ne0$ and $y\ne0$, this implies $g(z)=0$.

source.place: Tags 00IB (lemma-valuation-ring-x-or-x-inverse), 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian); direct agent coefficient-rescaling argument, not a proof attributed to ILO.

proof.text: Now $F(a+sz)=d\,h(sz)=ds\,g(z)=0$ and $(a+sz)-a=sz\in\mathfrak m_U$. Hence $a+sz\in U$ lifts the originally specified residue root $\alpha$. This proves the monic simple-root lifting property for $U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] implies that $U$ is henselian in the required idempotent-lifting sense. If $U=K$, its maximal ideal is zero and the branch $F(a)=0$ already supplies every lift; the same proof includes $V=U$ and $V=K$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q99-40773ce27 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all three cited statements, the report and the existing DAG neighbours in full. The delivery has no new nodes. The statement, source, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are unchanged. ILO XX 4.4 (p.374) is only motivation, and proof_origin.by=agent says so honestly. The statement is true as written: a coarsening of a henselian valuation ring is henselian, with no rank hypothesis. I checked all six steps. Steps 1 and 2 are elementary and correct: both rings are local by the x or x^{-1} condition; m_U is contained in m_V because x in m_U outside V would give x^{-1} in V, so x would be a unit of U; and a finite product of inverses s lies in V and is a unit of U. Step 3 uses the reverse direction of lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting for the local ring U: h=d^{-1}F(a+X) has linear coefficient 1 and c_0 in m_U, and the case F(a)=0 is split off. Step 4: I recomputed (y^n/b_0)g(b_0/y)=Q(y). Q is monic in V[Y] with reduction Y^{n-1}(Y+1), and its derivative at -1 is (-1)^{n-1}, so -1 is a simple root also in characteristic 2 and for n=1. Step 5 uses the forward direction for V and gives y congruent to -1, hence a unit of U, so z=b_0/y is in m_U and g(z)=0. Step 6 gives F(a+sz)=ds g(z)=0, and a+sz lifts the specified U-residue. I tested n=1 explicitly (Q=Y+1, root -e) and the cases V=U, U=K, V=K. No duplicate exists: I searched with rg -L for coarsening, overring and henselian valuation and read the four nearest nodes. This is not a re-split delivery, and no SGA source is used. I accept the tool use of lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting, the generic Hensel criterion for local rings.
